title: Generators
concept: A generator is a special function that can pause execution in the middle (Yield) and resume it later (Resume).

steps.title: Defining a generator function
steps.explanation:
The `function*` syntax marks this as a generator function.

**What is a generator?**
A regular function runs to completion once called (Run-to-completion), but a generator can pause partway through and resume later.

steps.title: Creating the generator object
steps.explanation:
Calling `counter()` does not run the function body — instead, it returns a **Generator object (Iterator)**.
This object gives you control over when the function executes.
steps.keyInsight: Calling a generator function = creating an Iterator, not running the function

steps.title: First next() call
steps.explanation:
Calling `gen.next()` starts the function for the first time.
'Start!' is logged, then execution pauses at `yield 1`.

**What is Yield?**
A keyword that pauses execution — handing control and a value back to the caller while keeping the execution context intact.

steps.title: Second next() call
steps.explanation:
Calling `gen.next()` again resumes from just after `yield 1`.
'Resumed!' is logged, then execution pauses again at `yield 2`.

steps.title: Third next() call — completion
steps.explanation:
The final `gen.next()` call.
'Done!' is logged, and since there are no more yields, `done: true` is returned.
steps.keyInsight: done: true = the generator has finished executing completely

quiz.question: What signal indicates that a generator function has fully finished executing?
quiz.explanation: When the IteratorResult object `{ value: ..., done: true }` is returned, it means there is no more code left to run.

misconceptions.wrong: Generators run concurrently like multiple threads
misconceptions.correct: No — they still run on a single thread.
misconceptions.why:
Generators only pass execution control back and forth (Cooperative Multitasking) — they don't run simultaneously.
Only one thing executes at a time.

keyTakeaway: Because you can pause and resume function execution, generators are useful for writing asynchronous code that reads like synchronous code (e.g., Redux-Saga).
